Reviewer: uma pool job review-4192, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review.

I read all five changed files and issue #3646. I used the current laws from `upstream/main`, at `e6849c5aea183b81135c8143955cc8c88a429a89`. That commit is the parent of this PR head. The local trial merge reported `Already up to date`; no merge commit was needed. The review used `.claude/worktrees/review-4192`.

The tools-only scope and the deferred app work are clear. `Refs #3646` is correct for this partial change. The larger diameter below 90 degrees has a decision record and tests. There are no UI changes, dependency changes, process changes, or changed goldens.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Check bodies against the full cutting shape.** `crates/tools/src/milling_cutter.rs:304` compares each body band with `diameter / 2`. The tool is narrower near a rounded tip. I used DC 50, KAPR 90, APMX 8, and `SCMT120408`. I extended the existing cutter body down to the tip, at radius 24.8. Both `resolve()` and `assembled()` accepted it. At z = 0.1, the returned tool reaches only radius 24.58729833462074. The body is outside the tool used for the checks. This can hide a collision. Class: body containment below the flute top. Check each complete band against the actual tool profile, or refuse bodies that cannot fit. Add tests for both bull-nose and round-insert cutters.

2. **[P1] Check every seat in the multi-seat cutter.** `crates/tools/src/milling_cutter.rs:294` reads only `r.cutting.diameter`. The resolver gets this value from the one mounted insert. I kept `CSW1_1` on DC 50 and moved `CSW1_2` to radius 40. The four-seat cutter still resolved to a tool of diameter 50. Its shared insert at the second seat reaches diameter 80. This can hide a gouge or collision. Class: incomplete seat geometry checks. Keep enough assembly data to check every declared seat. Check the cutting-point radius, height, and orientation, including the seats represented by a count. Refuse geometry that the derived tool cannot enclose. Pin a valid selected seat with an invalid second seat.

3. **[P1] Bind the derived cutter to the assembly insert.** `crates/tools/src/milling_cutter.rs:298` uses the derived corner without a check against the assembly corner. I derived the cutter from `SCMT120408`, then resolved the same assembly with `SCMT120400`. Both inserts fit the seats. `r.cutting.corner_r` was 0, but `assembled()` returned a tool with corner 0.8. The sharp insert reaches radius 25 at the tip. The returned tool reaches only 24.2 there. This can hide a gouge after an insert change. Class: inconsistent cutter and assembly inputs. Derive and resolve from the same checked component data, or refuse a mismatch. A diameter match alone does not make the two inputs consistent. Add a test that changes the shared insert before assembly.

Local results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed; 183 tools lib tests, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- After the mutation and probe sources were restored, `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib milling_cutter_tests`: passed; 7 tests, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: passed. All 11 light tests ran in 5 steps. There were 0 failures and 0 stalls. Each selected binary built in release mode.

Extra suites run:

- `review_probe_body_outside_rounded_corner_is_refused`: failed as described in finding 1.
- `review_probe_other_seat_outside_dc_is_refused`: failed as described in finding 2.
- `review_probe_different_assembly_insert_is_refused`: failed as described in finding 3.
- No fixture, importer, post, operation, motion, or example catalog file changed. The extra fixture/importer/catalog selection rules add no suite.

Mutations run locally:

- m1: use `DC` as the cutting diameter below 90 degrees. Red: 3 of the 7 PR tests failed.
- m2: use the cutting diameter as the shank diameter. Red: `the_tool_holds_the_real_cutter` failed.
- Restored source: all 7 PR tests passed. Temporary probe sources were also restored. No code or evidence was committed or pushed.

Goldens moved: none. No full heavy lane ran. No GitHub runner was used. The worktree and build outputs remain in place for the next review.

The Claude job environment variables are not set on this host. The job name above uses the assigned review task.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Reply to the review of head `25eca3ba4` (comment 7197613547). Commit `1366f4942` closes the three findings. The PR stays ready. The new head waits for a fresh review.

**1. Bodies against the full cutting shape (class: body containment below the flute top).**
- `MillingCutter::assembled` now checks each body band inside the cutting depth against the tool profile at the lowest point of the band. The profile includes the corner arc. The profile widens from the tip up, so the lowest point is the narrowest point.
- Pin: `a_body_outside_the_rounded_corner_is_refused`. The bull-nose case (Ø50, `SCMT120408`, body r 24.8 down to the tip) is refused, because the tool reaches r 24.2 there. The round-insert case (Ø32, `RCMT1204M0`, body r 15) is refused, because the tool reaches r 10 there. A body under the flat of the tip passes in both cases.
- Mutation m5: the check uses `diameter / 2` again. The pin is red.

**2. Every seat (class: incomplete seat geometry checks).**
- `assembled` now takes the assembly nodes and resolves them itself. It places each seat port of the body as the mounted insert is placed: the port frame, the mount turn and the cutting point of the insert.
- Each seat must put the cutting point on `DC` and in the tip plane (0.001 mm). Its axes, read in its own radial frame, must be the axes of the mounted seat. Thus each seat is the mounted seat turned about the spindle axis. A seat port with no frame is refused.
- A body with one seat port and a seat count: the other seats are copies of that port turned about the axis, so the check of the one port covers them.
- Pin: `every_seat_is_checked_not_only_the_mounted_one`. The selected seat `CSW1_1` is valid. `CSW1_2` on Ø80, `CSW1_3` 1 mm off the tip plane and `CSW1_4` turned 10 degrees are each refused by port (`SeatOff`). A one-port body with a seat count of 4 passes.
- Mutations m6, m7 and m8 remove the radius, height and orientation checks. Each one makes the pin red.

**3. One source for the derived cutter and the assembly (class: inconsistent cutter and assembly inputs).**
- The cutter now keeps the body and the insert that it was derived from. The assembly must mount exactly these two components (full equality, not a diameter match). Another insert or another body is refused by name (`Mismatch`).
- Pin: `an_assembly_with_other_components_is_refused`. The shared insert changes to `SCMT120400` before the assembly, under a cutter derived from `SCMT120408`. The assembly is refused. A cutter derived from another body is also refused.
- Mutations m9 and m10 remove the insert check and the body check. Each one makes the pin red.

**Readings.**
- Your three probes, in the old API, failed on `25eca3ba4` on winbuild (4 of 4 red, with a round-insert probe added). The new pins are the same cases in the new API.
- Gate on head `1366f4942` (the first line of `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-4192-1366f4942.log`), trial-merged with `origin/main` `72890060b`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` ran 1 step, `tools suites: lib`, with 186 passed and 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- The decision file and the PR body have the three rules, the pins and the mutation table.

Ready for a re-check.
